I've been working this land since I was 19. My mother farmed it before me, and I know every patch of it. I don't need a book to tell me what to do — the soil tells me, and so do my neighbors.

**My thinking:**

My 12 mu splits the way it always has. Nine mu goes into wheat-maize rotation — that's the backbone, that's what feeds us and pays the bills. I put the other 3 mu in cotton because the price has been decent, and I know cotton. It's hard work but I'm used to it.

For wheat, I'll do rotary tillage before planting in October, same as always. I use improved varieties — the seed seller in town has been pushing Jimai 22 and my neighbor Old Liu got good yields last year. I put down base fertilizer at planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate at sowing, at overwintering, at jointing, and at grain filling — four times is what I've always done with the well. Two rounds of pesticide: one for weeds early, one for aphids and rust near heading.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I drill the hybrid seed directly into the stubble — no turning the soil. Saves time and the tractor cost. I fertilize twice and water when I see the leaves start to roll. Three irrigations is usually enough unless summer is dry.

Cotton goes in the south field in April after frost. I'll plough that one deep because cotton roots need room. Bt hybrid seed — it handles bollworm better and I don't have to spray as much as my mother used to. But I still spray 8 times through the season for other pests and boll disease. Cotton needs a lot of water too, especially in July.
